facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is an extinct genus of large marine sauropterygian reptiles that lived during the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus (Greek: (), near to + (), lizard) is a genus of extinct, large marine sauropterygian reptile that lived during the Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: The genus Plesiosaurus contains only one valid species, Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus.
facts.quote: It contains only one species, the type, Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus.

facts.statement: The name Plesiosaurus was coined by William Conybeare and Henry De la Beche in 1821 based on scattered finds from the Bristol region, Dorset, and Lyme Regis.
facts.quote: Conybeare and De la Beche coined the name for scattered finds from the Bristol region, Dorset, and Lyme Regis in 1821.

facts.statement: The type species Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus was named and described by Conybeare in 1824 based on Mary Anning's original finds.
facts.quote: The type species of Plesiosaurus, P. dolichodeirus, was named and described by Conybeare in 1824 on the basis of Anning's original finds.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus possessed simple, needle-like cone teeth that were slightly curved and circular in cross-section.
facts.quote: The teeth of Plesiosaurus are "simple, needle-like cones" that are "slightly curved and circular in transverse section".

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus had between 20 and 25 teeth in each upper jaw row and 24 teeth in each lower jaw row.
facts.quote: There are 20 to 25 teeth per upper jaw tooth row, and 24 per low jaw tooth row.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus was a moderately sized plesiosaur growing to between 2.87 and 3.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus was a moderately sized plesiosaur that grew to 2.87 - 3.5 m in length.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus had approximately 40 cervical vertebrae, with preserved specimens showing counts between 38 and 42.
facts.quote: There are approximately 40 cervical vertebrae (neck vertebrae), with different specimens preserving 38 to 42 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus possessed gastralia, or belly ribs, with nine or more sets found between the shoulder and pelvis.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus also has gastralia, also known as "belly ribs." Nine or more sets of gastralia are present between the shoulder and pelvis.

facts.statement: In adult Plesiosaurus, the hindlimbs were long and narrow but much smaller than the forelimbs.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs are long and narrow, and in adults, they are much smaller than the forelimbs.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus has historically been treated as a wastebasket taxon containing many species that were later reassigned.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus has historically been a wastebasket taxon.

facts.statement: Review of Early Jurassic species indicates that Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus is the only English species properly assigned to the genus Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: Review of the Early Jurassic species indicates that the only English species properly assigned to Plesiosaurus is P. dolichodeirus.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is known from nearly complete skeletons found in the Lias formation of England.
facts.quote: It is known by nearly complete skeletons from the Lias of England.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus likely fed on belemnites, fish, and other prey.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus is thought to have eaten belemnites, fish and other prey.

facts.statement: The U-shaped jaw and sharp teeth of Plesiosaurus functioned like a fish trap.
facts.quote: Its U-shaped jaw and sharp teeth would have been like a fish trap.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus moved by paddling its flippers, as its tail was too short to be useful for propulsion.
facts.quote: It propelled itself by the paddles, the tail being too short to be of much use.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Plesiosaurus may have used its long neck as a rudder while navigating during chases.
facts.quote: Its neck could have been used as a rudder when navigating during a chase.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus gave birth to live young in the water, similar to most sea snakes.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus gave live birth to live young in the water like most sea snakes.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Plesiosaurus young lived in estuaries before moving into the open ocean.
facts.quote: The young might have lived in estuaries before moving out into the open ocean.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the long neck of Plesiosaurus hindered acceleration by creating turbulence when bent.
facts.quote: It has been postulated that the long neck of Plesiosaurus would have been a hindrance when trying to speed up, any bend in the neck creating turbulences.

facts.statement: Due to potential acceleration issues, Plesiosaurus may have hunted by lying in wait rather than pursuing prey.
facts.quote: For this reason it may be possible that these animals would actually lie in wait for prey to come close instead of trying to pursue them.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically from the Hettangian to Toarcian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Inferior (Hettangiense - Toarciense)

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is known from nearly complete skeletons found in the Lias of England.
facts.quote: es conocido de esqueletos casi completos del Lias de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is distinguished by its small head, long and thin neck, turtle-like wide body, short tail, and two pairs of large flippers.
facts.quote: Se distingue por su pequeña cabeza, su cuello largo y delgado, un cuerpo ancho como el de una tortuga, una cola corta, y dos pares de grandes aletas.

facts.statement: Compared to other plesiosaur genera, Plesiosaurus had a small head.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus tenía una cabeza pequeña.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus teeth were simple, needle-shaped cones slightly curved and circular in cross-section.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Plesiosaurus son simples, conos en forma de aguja levemente curvados y circulares en sección transversal.

facts.statement: All Plesiosaurus teeth were procumbent, especially those near the front, lying about 10-15 degrees above the horizontal.
facts.quote: Todos los dientes son procumbentes, especialmente aquellos más cercanos a la parte anterior, yaciendo cerca de 10-15° sobre el horizontal.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus was a medium-sized plesiosaur that grew to between 3 and 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus era un plesiosaurio de talla media que crecía entre 3 a 5 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus had approximately 40 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Tenía aproximadamente 40 vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus had about 21 dorsal vertebrae and at least three sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Cerca de 21 vértebras corresponden a las dorsales (de la espalda) y tenía al menos tres vértebras sacrales.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus possessed at least 28 caudal vertebrae, with a few more possibly located at the tail's end.
facts.quote: Posee al menos 28 vértebras caudales y unas pocas más pudieron haber estado en el final de la cola.

facts.statement: The genus Plesiosaurus was named by Conybeare in 1821.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Conybeare, 1821

facts.statement: P. dolichodirus is the type species of Plesiosaurus, described by Conybeare in 1824.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. dolichodirus (tipo) Conybeare, 1824

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus gave its name to the order Plesiosauria, of which it is a primitive but typical member.
facts.quote: Este animal dio nombre al orden Plesiosauria, de la cual es un miembro primitivo, pero típico.

facts.statement: The mandibular ramus of Plesiosaurus forms an almost perfect "V" at an angle of nearly 45 degrees with only a slight medial curvature.
facts.quote: El ramo mandibular forma una "V" casi perfecta en un ángulo de casi 45° con solo una leve curvatura medial.

facts.statement: A strongly fused symphysis pointed downward like a spoon, incorporating 2.5 small cavities in each ramus.
facts.quote: Una fuertemente fusionada sínfisis apuntando como una cuchara hacia abajo, incorporaba 2,5 pequeñas cavidades en cada rama.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus has traditionally been assigned a single tooth in the symphysis, like other long-necked genera.
facts.quote: A Plesiosaurus le ha sido tradicionalmente adjudicado un único diente en la sínfisis, así como a otros géneros de cuello largo.

facts.statement: The space between the rib arches from the posterior margin of the coracoid to the pubis is filled with pachyostotic gastralia.
facts.quote: El espacio entre los arcos de las costillas desde el margen posterior del coracoides al pubis está lleno de gastralias paquiostóticas.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus had paddle-shaped forelimbs with five complete digits but a very large number of phalanges on each.
facts.quote: Los miembros formaban aletas alargadas, en forma de remo con cinco dígitos completos, aunque cada uno consiste de un número muy grande de falanges.

facts.statement: Skin impressions suggest Plesiosaurus had smooth skin rather than scales.
facts.quote: Algunas impresiones de piel descubiertas sugieren que era lisa, no escamosa.

facts.statement: The ulna was a very wide, crescent-shaped plate while the robust radius was column-like.
facts.quote: El cúbito o ulna en forma de placa tiene forma de media luna y es muy ancho, mientras que el radio es robusto y en forma de columna.

facts.statement: In adults, the hind limbs were smaller than the forelimbs, though this difference was less obvious in juveniles.
facts.quote: Los miembros posteriores son menores que los anteriores en los individuos adultos pero esto no es tan obvio en los ejemplares menores.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus was among the first "antediluvian reptiles" discovered and generated great interest in Victorian England.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus fue uno de los primeros de los "reptiles antediluvianos" en ser descubiertos y generó un gran interés en la Inglaterra victoriana.

facts.statement: The name Plesiosaurus was coined in 1821 by Conybeare and De la Beche based on scattered materials from Lyme Regis, Dorest, and the Bristol region of England.
facts.quote: Conyebeare y De la Beche acuñaron el nombre basándose en materiales aislados y dispares de Lyme Regis, Dorest y la región de Bristol de Inglaterra en 1821.

facts.statement: The first specific description of Plesiosaurus was by Conybeare in 1824 for the type species P. dolichodeirus, based on a complete skeleton found by Mary Anning in December 1823 near Lyme Regis.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la primera descripción específica de Plesiosaurus y de un plesiosaurio fue la de la especie tipo P. dolichodeirus y fue hecha por Conyebeare en 1824 sobre un esqueleto completo hallado por Mary Anning) en diciembre de 1823 en el Lias Inferior (Sinemuriano) cerca de Lyme Regis.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is the archetypal genus of Plesiosauria and the first described, so the order derives its name from it.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus es el género arquetípico de Plesiosauria y el primero en ser descrito, por lo cual este orden deriva su nombre de Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: Hundreds of Plesiosaurus species were described worldwide without considering sample size or specimen quality.
facts.quote: Cientos de especies de Plesiosaurus fueron descritas en todo el mundo sin considerar el tamaño de la muestra o la calidad del espécimen.

facts.statement: P. dolichodeirus is the only species of the genus based on appropriate and diagnosed material.
facts.quote: P. dolichodeirus es la única especie del género basada en material apropiado y diagnosticado.

facts.statement: Species like P. brachypterygius, P. guilielmiiperatoris, and P. tournemirensis were moved to new genera Hydrorion, Seeleyosaurus, and Occitanosaurus respectively.
facts.quote: P. brachypterygius, P. guilielmiiperatoris y P. tournemirensis, por ejemplo, tuvieron que ser clasificados en nuevos géneros, Hydrorion, Seeleyosaurus y Occitanosaurus, respectivamente.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus belongs to the parent group Plesiosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Plesiosauroidea

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus lived from the Rhaetian to the Maastrichtian, between 205.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Maastrichtian (205.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: English coasts have exposed canteras from the Lower Jurassic Lias Group that produced many of the most important known plesiosaur specimens.
facts.quote: Las costas inglesas han expuesto canteras pertenecientes predominantemente al Grupo Lias del Jurásico Inferior que han producido muchos de los especímenes de plesiosaurio más importantes conocidos.

facts.statement: Many P. dolichodeirus specimens were found in the Lyme Regis area and remain restricted to that environment.
facts.quote: Numerosos especímenes de Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus estuvieron entre estos hallazgos. Estos especímenes permanecen restringidos a los entornos de Lyme Regis.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus fed on belemnites, fish, and other prey.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurus se alimentaba de belemnites, peces y otras presas.

facts.statement: Its U-shaped jaws and sharp teeth may have acted as a trap for fish.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas en forma de U y dientes agudos pudieron haber sido como una trampa para peces.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurus propelled itself with its flippers because its tail was too short to be a locomotor organ.
facts.quote: Se propulsaba con sus aletas, ya que su cola era demasiado corta como para ser un órgano locomotor.

facts.statement: Its neck may have been used as a rudder when swimming during a chase.
facts.quote: Su cuello pudo haberse usado como un timón cuando navegaba durante una persecución.

facts.statement: Based on findings in the Cretaceous plesiosaur Polycotylus, Plesiosaurus surely gave birth to its young in the water like sea snakes.
facts.quote: Basándose en hallazgos hechos en el plesiosaurio cretácico Polycotylus, Plesiosaurus seguramente daba a luz a sus crías en el agua como las serpientes marinas.

facts.statement: Juveniles may have lived in estuaries before moving to the open ocean.
facts.quote: Los jóvenes pudieron haber vivido en estuarios antes de irse al océano abierto.

facts.statement: None of the hundreds of Jurassic and Cretaceous plesiosaurs referred to Plesiosaurus were correctly assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: De los cientos de plesiosaurios del Jurásico y el Cretácico referidos a Plesiosaurus, ninguno fue correctamente asignado.
